Subject: PR #302: Schema migration safety check for [ORG_1] Core API v2

Hi [PERSON_1],

I'm reviewing your Django migration in PR #302 where you are dropping the `old_auth_token` column from the user model. 

Since we are using a blue-green deployment strategy, we need to be extremely careful here. During the deployment window on [DATE_1], both the old version of the codebase (which still references `old_auth_token` in its ORM models) and the new codebase will be running simultaneously. If we drop the database column first, the old app instances will immediately start throwing 500 errors because Django's internal SELECT queries will look for a column that no longer exists.

Can we split this into three safe phases instead?
- Phase 1 (This PR): Mark the field as deprecated in Django, remove all active code references to it, but keep the column in the DB.
- Phase 2: Deploy Phase 1 and ensure all old instances are decommissioned.
- Phase 3 (Next Sprint): Run a separate migration to safely drop the column.

Let me know your thoughts.

Best,
[PERSON_2]

Subject: PR #712: Flyway migration V4.2.1__add_org_billing_limits

Hey [PERSON_1],

Thanks for putting together the Flyway migration for the new billing limits. The schema change itself looks perfect, but I noticed a small issue with the migration metadata naming convention.

Our current schema version in master is already at `V4.2.3`. Your script is named `V4.2.1__add_org_billing_limits.sql`. If we try to merge this, Flyway will throw an out-of-order execution error during the CI pipeline run.

Please rename the migration file to `V4.2.4__add_org_billing_limits.sql` so it appends correctly to the migration sequence. 

Also, just as a reminder, please run `./gradlew flywayValidate` locally to ensure the checksum is correct before pushing your next commit.

Cheers,
